forecast-period.text: A low pressure system near Yorke Peninsula and an associated vigorous cold front will continue to move eastwards this evening and overnight before moving out over the eastern states early Monday morning. A high pressure system moves just to the north on Monday, ahead of another cold front forecast to move across South Australia on Tuesday. Another ridge of high pressure pushes into the west of the state on Wednesday, with the associated high moving over South Australia on Thursday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible patchy morning frost about the Flinders Ranges and northwest of SA. Scattered showers about the agricultural area, becoming isolated during the morning, then contracting to windward coasts and ranges during the afternoon, before redeveloping about western and southern coasts during the late evening. Maximum temperatures generally below average, but tending near average about the southeast. West to southwesterly winds, tending northwesterly in the west during the afternoon and evening. Winds fresh to strong about central and eastern coasts and ranges during the morning.

Areas of rain across the state, tending to scattered showers from the west, gradually contracting to the agricultural areas and south of the pastoral districts during the evening. Gusty thunderstorms about the agricultural area and south of the Pastoral districts. Possible raised dust in the northeast. Locally heavy falls possible about the Fleurieu Peninsula and with thunderstorms. Fresh to strong and gusty west to southwesterly winds extending throughout. Winds possibly severe about Eyre Peninsula, windward coasts of Yorke Peninsula and the Flinders Ranges. Southwesterly winds moderating from the west during the afternoon and evening.

Possible morning fog and frost about the northern agricultural area and parts of the Pastoral districts. Showers about the agricultural area,possibly extending into the south of the Pastoral districts. Showers more frequent about southern and western coasts. Possible thunderstorms about windward coasts and about the Flinders Ranges. Maximum temperatures near average about the coastal fringe but tending below average elsewhere. Freshening north to northwesterly winds ahead of a fresh and gusty southwesterly change extending eastwards during the day.

Possible morning frost about the northern agricultural area and parts of the Pastoral districts. Showers about the agricultural area, possibly extending into the south of the pastoral districts, contracting to windward coasts and ranges during the evening. Maximum temperatures below average. West to southwesterly winds, fresh about coastal parts and in the northeast, easing during the day. Winds tending southwest to southeasterly from the west during the day.

text.p: Possible morning frost about the northern agricultural area and parts of the Pastoral districts. Isolated showers about the agricultural area, mainly about windward coasts and ranges. Maximum temperatures below average, tending slightly above average about the southern agricultural area. Southwest to southeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: Falls of 2 to 10 mm about the west coast and south of the pastoral districts, increasing 10 to 20 mm about the agricultural areas, Eyre Peninsula, Flinders Ranges and south of the Pastoral districts, and increasing further to 20 to 30 mm about western facing coasts and ranges. Local falls of 30 to 60 mm are possible about the Mount Lofty Ranges and with thunderstorms. Less than 2 mm about the north.
